title: Family of homicide victim Trina Hunt files civil lawsuit against her husband
summary: The lawsuit, filed by Trina's mother, brother and sister-in-law, asks the B.C. Supreme Court to declare that Iain Hunt killed his wife Trina, and make him hand over any property he inherited from her…

image.caption: The remains of Port Moody woman Trina Hunt, 48, were found near Hope, B.C., in March 2021. Now, her family is seeking to have a court declare that her husband Iain killed Trina, and make him hand over any property he inherited. (Twitter/Port Moody Police)

Lawsuit asks court to declare that Iain Hunt killed his wife, make him hand over any property he inherited
A civil lawsuit has been filed against Iain Hunt, the husband of homicide victim Trina Hunt, who was charged with indignity to human remains in relation to her death.

The lawsuit, filed by Trina's mother, brother and sister-in-law, asks the B.C. Supreme Court to declare that Iain killed Trina, and make him hand over any property he inherited from her after her death.
Trina's remains were found near Hope, B.C., in March 2021 — two months after her husband reported her missing from her house in Port Moody.
Police charged him with indignity to human remains in relation to her death, which police have said is a homicide. However, no murder or manslaughter charges have been laid in the case.
Iain Hunt is seen in December 2018. He was charged in February 2025 with one count of indignity to human remains in relation to his wife's death. (Ben Nelms/CBC)
The civil lawsuit states that Iain intentionally misled Trina's family by reporting Trina missing, even though he knew where her body was.

"Mr. Hunt continued the charade by initially participating in a reward for information concerning Trina's disappearance and continuing to assert he knew nothing of her death when he knew all the time that Trina was dead, and he knew the location of her body," the lawsuit states.

blocks.text: The notice of civil claim said that the family relied on Iain's statements as being truthful, which led to concerted public efforts to find the Port Moody woman and raise awareness of her case.
Before Trina Hunt's remains were found, supporters organized extensive search efforts as well as online and in-person campaigns to raise awareness of her case.
Online court records show Iain allegedly interfered with his wife's remains on Jan. 16, 2021, two days before he reported her missing.
Family and supporters of Trina Hunt are seen outside a Port Coquitlam courthouse in March 2025, during an appearance by Iain Hunt. (Ben Nelms/CBC)
'Mental anguish and distress'

The lawsuit says that Iain's actions continue to cause the family "mental anguish and distress," and it seeks special damages for funeral costs and other costs, in addition to making the court hand over any property he inherited.

In the notice of civil claim, Trina's family claims Iain sold the property he co-owned with his wife in May 2023 for $1.92 million, and subsequently bought a property in the rural Fraser Valley community of Harrison Mills.
The family says that property was bought with the funds he obtained by selling the Port Moody house, which he bought with his wife in 2006 for just over $632,000.
Trina's family is seeking a certificate of pending litigation against the Harrison Mills property, as well as a tracing order for all the assets he inherited from Trina after her "wrongful death."

Frank Jang with the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team (IHIT) holds up a picture of Trina Hunt during a May 2021 news conference. Police have said Trina's death is a homicide, but no one has been charged with murder or manslaughter in relation to her death. (Ben Nelms/CBC)

A charge of indignity to human remains "occurs when a person neglects to perform their legal duty to bury a dead human body, or if a person interferes in an improper, indecent or undignified way with a dead human body or human remains," according to police.
None of the lawsuit's allegations have been proven in court.
Iain Hunt's next court appearance, in relation to the indignity to human remains charge, is in September 2027.
